items.question: I broadcast a 'follow' custom_json (alice follows bob) signed with alice's ACTIVE key: required_auths = ['alice'], required_posting_auths = []. The transaction is in an irreversible block and RC was charged, but bridge.get_relationship_between_accounts still reports follows = false and the follow never appears. Is hivemind lagging?
items.expected: No. Hivemind only processes social custom_jsons that carry exactly one required_posting_auths entry and zero required_auths; the follow processor (and the reblog, notify and community processors) silently skip everything else, even though the op is valid on L1. Re-broadcast with the posting authority (required_posting_auths = ['alice']) and keep the payload's follower equal to that auth account.
forbidden: hivemind is still syncing; wait for the block to become irreversible
active authority is a superset of posting, so the follow will be indexed
follows must be sent under the 'reblog' id

items.question: bridge.get_post for a very popular post returns exactly 1000 entries in active_votes, yet the post has several thousand voters. Is the API node truncating, or is my client mis-parsing the array?
items.expected: Neither is broken: hivemind hardcodes a 1000-vote cap. Both post-object builders (bridge and condenser) call list_votes with limit 1000, database_api.find_votes does too, and database_api.list_votes only accepts limit in [1, 1000], so no single response ever lists more than 1000 votes for a post. Use the post's counters (bridge stats.total_votes, condenser net_votes) for totals, and page database_api.list_votes (order by_comment_voter, start [author, permlink, last_voter]) to enumerate beyond 1000.
forbidden: pass a larger limit to get_post to receive all votes
the post really has only 1000 votes
the node operator misconfigured the vote limit
items.origin: findings part 06 discovery 3; reference/hivemind/README.md Key Numbers

items.question: For the same post, condenser_api.get_content returns author_reputation as a 15-digit integer while bridge.get_post returns author_reputation as a number in the 70s. Which endpoint is broken?
items.expected: Neither. Condenser post objects emit the raw reputation bigint, while bridge post objects (and bridge.get_profile) apply rep_log10 = (log10(rep) - 9) * 9 + 25, which maps 0 to 25 and a 15-digit value into the 70s. Convert condenser/follow/tags values client-side with the same formula and never apply it again to bridge values.
forbidden: the bridge value is wrong or truncated
condenser is returning rshares instead of reputation
apply rep_log10 to the bridge value as well
items.origin: reference/hivemind/README.md non-obvious facts (API behavior: two reputation formulas)

items.question: A paid-out post set a 50% beneficiary. bridge.get_post reports author_payout_value roughly double what the author's author_reward_operation shows they actually received. Is hivemind's payout mirror corrupt?
items.expected: No, it is deliberate legacy behavior: hivemind computes author_payout_value = payout - curator_payout_value, and its stored payout is the vop total (author + curator + beneficiary), so the beneficiary share is reported inside author_payout_value (condenser's total_payout_value is derived the same way). The stored mirror itself is correct; subtract the beneficiary share yourself or read the comment_reward/author_reward virtual ops for the author-only amount.
forbidden: author_payout_value excludes beneficiary rewards
hivemind double-counts the curator cut
the payout mirror is only wrong for pre-HF19 posts

items.question: Which custom_json ids does hivemind 1.28.6 actually index, and what happens to custom_json operations with any other id?
items.expected: Exactly four ids: follow, reblog, community and notify (reblog payloads are accepted under either the follow or the reblog id). Every other custom_json id is dropped at the staging filter (load_ops_staging keeps op 18 only for those ids via HAF's custom_json_type_id, and the partial index is created for that array at sync start), so it never touches hivemind state.
forbidden: every custom_json id is indexed into a generic table
only follow and community are interpreted
the rc id is also interpreted by hivemind
items.origin: reference/hivemind/README.md non-obvious facts (API behavior: only four custom_json ids)

items.question: What JSON-RPC error does hivemind return when I call a method name that does not exist inside a known namespace, for example bridge.get_postz?
items.expected: Code -32602 (not the standard -32601) with message 'Assert Exception:unknown method: ...' and a data payload fabricated to look like a hived assert_exception (code 10, name assert_exception, a fake stack frame and an assert_hash). Only an unknown namespace such as foo.bar yields -32601 'Api not found foo', without the fabricated data.
forbidden: -32601 Method not found
an HTTP 404 from PostgREST
-32600 Invalid Request

items.question: What are the parameter defaults and allowed ranges for bridge.account_notifications, and how far back in time can it return notifications?
items.expected: account is required; min_score defaults to 25 and must be in [0, 100]; limit defaults to 100 and must be in [1, 100]; last_id is an exclusive cursor for descending pagination. Results are floored at 90 days before head (block_before_head('90 days')), matching the 90-day retention of hive_notification_cache.
forbidden: limit defaults to 20 with a maximum of 1000
min_score defaults to 0

items.question: Calling bridge.get_ranked_posts with limit = 100 fails with 'limit = 100 outside valid range [1:20]'. What is the real maximum page size for hivemind post lists, and can my client raise it?
items.expected: Post-list limits are validated against the hivemind_app.max_posts_per_call GUC, default 20 (the default limit is least(20, GUC)); valid_number raises on out-of-range values instead of clamping. Only the node operator can change it (ALTER DATABASE ... SET hivemind_app.max_posts_per_call), so a client must paginate with start_author / start_permlink.
forbidden: the maximum is 100
values above the maximum are silently clamped to 20
pass a page or offset parameter

items.question: I join hivemind_app.hive_posts.created_at against HAF block timestamps to find the block that created each post, and every match lands one block too early. Why, and what should I join on instead?
items.expected: Hivemind deliberately stamps real operations (comment, vote, ...) with the PREVIOUS block's timestamp, replicating the old Python _head_block_date behavior, so created_at / updated_at / last_update are 3 seconds earlier than the true L1 block time (only virtual-op-derived times are exact). Join on hive_posts.block_num_created, which is the creating block and does not move on edits (block_num does).
forbidden: hivemind stores the previous block's number, so subtract one from block_num
it is clock skew between the HAF node and hivemind
created_at equals the block timestamp; the join is wrong for another reason

items.question: My HAF app reads hivemind_app.hive_posts.muted_reasons to reproduce bridge's stats.muted_reasons, but for some posts bridge lists reasons 3 or 4 that the column never contains. Where do they come from?
items.expected: Only bits 0-2 (MUTED_COMMUNITY_MODERATION, MUTED_COMMUNITY_TYPE, MUTED_PARENT) are stored; bits 3 MUTED_REPUTATION and 4 MUTED_ROLE_COMMUNITY are appended at read time by create_bridge_post_object: 3 when the author is grayed (hive_accounts_view.is_grayed, reputation <= -464800000000) and 4 when the author's role in the post's community is -2 (muted). Reproduce them by joining the reputation view and hive_roles, not by reading the column.
forbidden: the column is stale; re-sync hivemind
bits 3 and 4 are written by community mutePost operations
stats.muted_reasons is just the decoded column
